notes: Perfect agreement on sensor development claims (C3, C43-C46). Both evaluators affirm the successful development and characterization of four new iDrugSnFRs with comprehensive dose-response data. Peer reviewers describe this as 'potentially a major advance for the field.'

Agreement on crystallographic structure claims (C4, C29-C37), though peer review groups additional claims including candle snuffer mechanism (C38-C42) and ligand binding details (C128-C129). Both affirm the quality and significance of the structural work at atomic resolution.

Agreement on 'candle snuffer' mechanism claims (C38-C43, C135-C143). LLM evaluates mechanism separately while peer review combines with structural claims. Both support the mechanistic interpretation based on structural data showing Glu78 movement and pH-dependence.

Agreement on specificity characterization (C47-C56). Both evaluators accept the comprehensive selectivity testing and cross-reactivity profiles. Peer reviewers praise characterization of 'sensitivity, selectivity, and kinetics' without raising concerns.

Perfect agreement on thermodynamic characterization by ITC (C57-C61). Both evaluators accept the KD/EC50 agreement and thermodynamic profiles without question. Peer review implicitly accepts this as part of comprehensive sensor characterization.

Agreement on stopped-flow kinetic analysis (C62-C67). Both accept the non-pseudo-first-order behavior and complex binding kinetics. Peer review groups these with microperfusion data (C68-C79) and affirms 'relatively fast time resolution.'

Agreement on microperfusion kinetic experiments (C68-C78). Both evaluators support the quantitative kinetic data and temporal resolution assessments. Peer reviewers explicitly affirm utility for tracking drugs with fast time resolution.

Strong agreement on cellular imaging at PM and ER (C5, C80-C96). Both evaluators support the detection of drugs at different subcellular compartments with differential kinetics. Peer reviewers praise 'utility in plasma membrane and ER sensing in neurons and cell lines.'

Agreement on >30-fold difference in membrane crossing rates (C7, C101, C146). Both evaluators accept the membrane permeability measurements and correlation with logDpH7.4 values. Peer review implicitly supports through praise of tracking drug permeation utility.

Agreement on validation that slow ER kinetics reflect membrane permeability (C97-C100). Both accept the nicotine control experiments demonstrating sensor functionality. Peer reviewers accept membrane permeability measurements as valid without challenge.

Agreement on novelty claims for time-resolved measurements of low logDpH7.4 drugs (C102, C110-C112). Both evaluators accept these methodological advances. Peer reviewers describe work as 'major advance for the field.'

Agreement on structure-function relationships for ligand binding (C128-C132). Both evaluators accept the high-resolution structural data showing cation-π interactions and hydrogen bonding. Peer review groups with broader structural claims.

Agreement on methodological advantages of iDrugSnFR paradigm (C113-C120). Both evaluators support the demonstrated sensitivity, ER targeting capability, and practical advantages. Peer reviewers affirm tools' utility and significance.

Disagreement on solution exchange limiting PM response rates (C6). LLM marks UNCERTAIN due to stated exceptions and inferential nature of evidence. Peer reviewers implicitly accept this as part of overall membrane permeability findings without raising concerns.

Agreement on varenicline binding characteristics (C121-C124). Both evaluators accept the unexpected high-affinity binding and role of His68. Peer review groups with broader specificity characterization without challenging these specific findings.

Disagreement on smoking cessation drug development implications (C147-C150). LLM marks UNCERTAIN noting significant speculation beyond experimental data. Peer reviewers accept these interpretive claims as reasonable inferences without challenge.

Agreement on uncertainty for future application predictions (C118, C127, C153). LLM marks as speculative extrapolations requiring validation. Peer reviewers also express uncertainty, requesting authors 'frame the bigger picture' and develop broader applicability claims more fully.

Peer review evaluates background/contextual claims (C1-C2, C8-C28) about smoking cessation drugs and membrane permeability principles. LLM did not produce a separate result for these framing claims. Peer reviewers implicitly accept as accurate context.
